title: Minimum Box Capacity to Ship Products
description_html:
You are a logistics manager shipping products from a warehouse. Each product type has a quantity and a weight per item. Shipping boxes have two constraints:

  • Capacity limit — maximum number of items per box.
  • Weight limit — maximum weight (kg) per box (maxWeightPerBox).

Rules:

  • Each product type must be packed separately.
  • All boxes share the same capacity and weight limits.
  • A box holds at most capacity items OR maxWeightPerBox kg, whichever comes first.
  • Items are whole numbers (no fractional items).

Given quantities, weights (kg per item), maxBoxes and maxWeightPerBox, return the minimum box capacity needed to ship all products within maxBoxes boxes.

Example 1

quantities = [8, 12, 5], weights = [2, 3, 1], maxBoxes = 6, maxWeightPerBox = 20
Output: 5

With capacity 5:
  P0 (8 @ 2kg): min(5, 20//2=10, 8) = 5/box -> 2 boxes
  P1 (12 @ 3kg): min(5, 20//3=6, 12) = 5/box -> 3 boxes
  P2 (5 @ 1kg): min(5, 20, 5) = 5/box -> 1 box
  Total = 6 boxes <= 6

Example 2

quantities = [10, 15, 8], weights = [5, 2, 3], maxBoxes = 10, maxWeightPerBox = 15
Output: 4

With capacity 4:
  P0 (10 @ 5kg): min(4, 15//5=3) = 3/box -> 4 boxes
  P1 (15 @ 2kg): min(4, 15//2=7) = 4/box -> 4 boxes
  P2 (8 @ 3kg): min(4, 15//3=5) = 4/box -> 2 boxes
  Total = 10 boxes <= 10

Approach

Binary search on the answer (capacity) with a simulated feasibility check. The predicate "capacity X works" is monotone — bigger capacity never needs more boxes. The check is NOT a closed-form division: each box is bounded by multiple interacting caps, so the effective items per box = min(capacity, floor(maxWeightPerBox / weight)) and boxes for a product = ceil(quantity / perBox); sum over products and compare to maxBoxes. Search capacity in [1, max(quantities)].

def min_capacity(quantities, weights, maxBoxes, maxWeightPerBox):
    def boxes(cap):
        t = 0
        for q, w in zip(quantities, weights):
            per = min(cap, maxWeightPerBox // w)
            if per == 0: return float("inf")
            t += -(-q // per)
        return t
    lo, hi = 1, max(quantities)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if boxes(mid) <= maxBoxes: hi = mid
        else: lo = mid + 1
    return lo

Pattern: bs-on-answer-compound (binary search on answer, simulated/compound-constraint feasibility). Related: LC 875, 1011, 410, 1283.
